newsitem.title: SPAIN: Zinc price rise boosts Asturiana H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Zinc price rise boosts Asturiana H1 profits.

text.p: Spanish zinc producer Asturiana de Zinc which turned to profit in the first half, highlighted a strengthening of its two key variables, the dollar and zinc prices.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Asturiana said the dollar had appreciated to 147.34 pesetas at the end of June from 130.45 pesetas at the beginning of the year, to give an average price of 142.42 pesetas over the period.
Meanwhile, zinc prices rose to $1,423 per tonne from $1,037 to give an average price of $1,236.42.
Asturiana posted a first half attributable profit of 2.93 billion pesetas after a 751 million peseta loss a year earlier.
The company said its international presence had improved over the period with the help of its main shareholder Glencore with contracts in new zinc plant projects.
Spain's stock market watchdog CNMV gave Glencore the green light in July to purchase a further 20 percent stake in Asturiana, bringing its total holding to 44.79 percent.
The zinc producer said its mining activities had contributed 18 percent to gross profit and had reached record lows for production costs.

In metallurgy, the tonne per worker ratio rose to 212.4 in the first half from 197.5 in 1996. Asturiana has made a number of investments in the sector including a new absorption column for reducing sulfuric anhydride emissions from its acid plants.
Asturiana said it had made a provision of 630 million pesetas in its results to correct the value of its stake in property firm Urbis which was valued at 1,415 pesetas per share on June 30.
